sentences.text: Researchers developed a mouse model in which rod photoreceptor cells express a fluorescent sensor to detect glutamate, allowing them to identify single vesicle release events. These measurements revealed that glutamate release from rod cells occurred randomly at a rate between 20 and 40 vesicles per second per ribbon, a finding consistent with independent electrical measurements suggesting a rate of about 38 vesicles per second per ribbon.

The study found that glutamate release from rods filtered out rapid changes, with signal power dropping as frequency increased from 1 to 10 Hz. The authors suggest that maintaining constant release rates across different light levels helps transmit light adaptation signals to the next neurons, stating that this specific mouse line is a useful tool for studying how light information is processed at the first synapse in the retina.
